platform_name: IETF LAMPS Composite Signatures Reference Implementation
product_name: IETF LAMPS Composite Signatures Reference Implementation
product_brief: RFC 10073 defines Composite ML-DSA, a PQ/T hybrid signature scheme combining ML-DSA with RSA, ECDSA, Ed25519 and Ed448 for X.509/PKIX.
pqc_support: Yes — Composite ML-DSA (ML-DSA combined with traditional algorithms) specified as a Standards Track RFC for X.509/PKIX
pqc_capability_description: RFC 10073 specifies Composite ML-DSA, a PQ/T hybrid signature scheme pairing FIPS 204 ML-DSA (44/65/87) with RSASSA-PSS, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, ECDSA, Ed25519 or Ed448 as a single atomic algorithm. Defines key generation, ASN.1 modules, OIDs, key/signature sizes, and test vectors. Offers EUF-CMA (not SUF-CMA) security.
crypto_primitives: ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65, ML-DSA-87, RSASSA-PSS, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, ECDSA (P-256, P-384, P-521, brainpoolP256r1, brainpoolP384r1), Ed25519, Ed448, SHA-256, SHA-384, SHA-512, SHAKE256
signature_schemes: Composite ML-DSA (ML-DSA with RSASSA-PSS, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, ECDSA, Ed25519, Ed448); e.g. id-MLDSA65-ECDSA-P256-SHA512, id-MLDSA44-Ed25519-SHA512, id-MLDSA87-ECDSA-P384-SHA512
testing_&_validation_methods: Test vectors in an ACVP/KAT-like format are provided in Appendix E for each composite and for ML-DSA in isolation, covering signature verification, certificate validation, and signing; a Python reference implementation generated them.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Does not provide application backwards compatibility; only upgraded systems understand the new OIDs. Composites fit into existing systems as a signature algorithm, and the document recommends profiling the many combinations down.

evidence.PQC Support: This document defines a PQ/T hybrid scheme with concrete instantiations that combine the US NIST Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) with traditional algorithms
evidence.PQC Capability Description: The composite algorithm presents a single public key and signature value such that it can be treated as a single atomic algorithm at the protocol level.
evidence.FIPS Validated: This guidance is not authoritative and has not been endorsed by US NIST.
evidence.Crypto Primitives: Instantiations of the Composite ML-DSA scheme are provided based on ML-DSA, RSASSA-PSS, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, ECDSA, Ed25519, and Ed448.
evidence.Hybrid Sig Support: This specification creates PQ/T hybrids with the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA), defined in [ FIPS.204 ] as the Post-Quantum (PQ) component.

product_brief: Pure Rust, no_std wrapper crate implementing the FN-DSA (Falcon-based) post-quantum signature algorithm: key generation, signing and verification.
pqc_support: Yes — FN-DSA signature scheme (key generation, signing, verification), though the standard is still in draft and not yet published
pqc_capability_description: Implements FN-DSA key pair generation, signature generation and verification, with degrees 512 (logn=9) and 1024 (logn=10) plus weak/test degrees 2–8. The FN-DSA standard is only being drafted; keys may not interoperate with the final standard. Pre-1.0 implementation.
crypto_primitives: FN-DSA (Falcon); SHA3-224/256/384/512; SHAKE128/SHAKE256; SHA-256/384/512 and SHA-512-256 (as hash identifiers)
primary_platforms: x86 (32-bit and 64-bit, with AVX2 acceleration), x86_64 and ARMv8 (aarch64, arm64ec) with native floating-point; portable floating-point emulation on other platforms; embedded systems (no_std)
pqc_roadmap_details: Implementation is expected to be adjusted to the FN-DSA standard when published, before the 1.0 version release.
implementation_attack_surface: Native hardware floating-point on x86_64 and aarch64 assumed constant-time for non-exceptional inputs; portable floating-point emulation makes a best effort at constant-time, though recent compiler optimizations might introduce variable-time operations. Keygen and verification use no floating-point.
testing_&_validation_methods: Unit tests exist; an internal unit test checks that the sampler returns the same values as the original Falcon code for the same inputs.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: no_std compatible; split sub-crates (fn-dsa-kgen, fn-dsa-sign, fn-dsa-vrfy) reduce code footprint for embedded systems that only verify signatures.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Open-source Rust crate; no external dependencies except rand_core and zeroize (unit tests use a few extra crates).
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Key encodings, message pre-hashing and domain separation may change when the final FN-DSA standard is published; generated key pairs may fail to interoperate with the final standard.

evidence.PQC Support: This crate is really a wrapper for the fn-dsa-kgen , fn-dsa-sign and fn-dsa-vrfy crates that implement the various elements of the FN-DSA signature algorithm.
evidence.PQC Capability Description: Key pairs generated with this crate MAY fail to be interoperable with the final FN-DSA standard.
evidence.Signature Schemes: Symbolic constant for FN-DSA with degree 1024 ( logn = 10 ).
evidence.PQC Roadmap Details: This implementation is expected to be adjusted to the FN-DSA standard when published (before the 1.0 version release).

product_brief: C implementation of FN-DSA, the upcoming NIST post-quantum signature scheme based on Falcon, covering keygen, signing and verification.
pqc_support: Yes — FN-DSA (Falcon-based) signature scheme; implementation tracks a best-guess of the FIPS 206 draft, which has not yet been published
pqc_capability_description: Implements FN-DSA (based on Falcon), a post-quantum signature scheme being defined by NIST. Provides key pair generation, signature generation and verification. Not the "real" FN-DSA since no draft is published; adjusted to a best guess of the FIPS 206 draft. Backward compatibility not guaranteed until version 1.0. Reproduces the same test vectors as the Rust implementation.
primary_platforms: Windows and Unix-like systems (Linux, macOS); ARM Cortex-M4F (STM32F407G-DISC1 board); bare metal via caller-supplied seed
pqc_roadmap_details: Implementation will be adjusted when the FN-DSA/FIPS 206 draft and final standard are published; backward compatibility is not maintained until version 1.0, which will be published only after the final FN-DSA standard.
testing_&_validation_methods: Test suite (test_fndsa.c, test_sign.c) and benchmarks (speed_fndsa.c); reproduces same test vectors as the Rust implementation (interoperable)
qrng_&_entropy_sources: Uses the operating system's RNG on Windows and Unix-like systems; caller may supply a seed for unsupported systems, with at least 256 bits of entropy recommended
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: ARM Cortex-M4F assembly routines for speed-ups; temporary buffers can be provided externally for small embedded systems with shallow stacks; benchmark app for the STM32F407G-DISC1 board
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Open-source C variant of the Rust implementation; verify-only apps can omit kgen and sign files to reduce footprint
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Backward compatibility explicitly NOT maintained before version 1.0; keys and signatures may cease to be accepted by later versions

evidence.PQC Support: FN-DSA is a new upcoming post-quantum signature scheme, currently being defined by NIST as part of their Post-Quantum Cryptography Standardization project.
evidence.PQC Capability Description: This code has been adjusted to match my best guess of what the FIPS 206 (FN-DSA) draft will contain.
evidence.Signature Schemes: FN-DSA is based on the Falcon scheme.
evidence.PQC Roadmap Details: Only version 1.0 will provide such stability, and it will be published only after publication of the final FN-DSA standard.
